The manipulation of time in the story is handled with great skill, balancing both compression and stretching to serve the emotional arc of the narrative. 

**Compression** is used effectively to convey the lingering, repetitive nature of Daniel's dreams and the passage of seasons. The story opens by summarizing "several months" of dreams into a few paragraphs, and later effortlessly skips from October to April in a single sentence transition ("In April, they rented one..."). Similarly, nine years of a past marriage and four years of a current relationship are compressed into brief, poignant summaries that give the reader just enough context without bogging down the present narrative.

Conversely, the author slows the pace down—**stretching** time—for the moments that carry the most psychological and emotional weight. The moment Daniel finds the keys in the closet is stretched out; the narrative lingers on the physical sensation of the cold metal and the faded tag, expanding a few seconds of real-time into a multi-paragraph flashback of the apartment and the canoe trip with Rachel. The story also slows down to play out scenes of dialogue at the breakfast table and on the river in real-time, allowing the subtle, tender dynamics between Daniel and Isabel to breathe and develop naturally. This rhythm of summarizing the routine passage of time while lingering on moments of quiet revelation makes the story's pacing feel entirely earned and balanced.
